spots.name: British Columbia Parliament Buildings
spots.summary: The British Columbia Parliament Buildings are in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada, and are home to the lieutenant governor and the Legislative Assembly.

spots.name: The Empress
spots.summary: The Fairmont Empress, formerly and commonly referred to as The Empress, is one of the oldest hotels in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada. Located on 721 Government Street, it is situated in Downtown Victoria, facing the city's Inner Harbour.

spots.name: Royal British Columbia Museum
spots.summary: The Royal British Columbia Museum, founded in 1886, is a history museum in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada. The "Royal" title was approved by Queen Elizabeth II and bestowed by Prince Philip in 1987, to coincide with a royal tour of that year. The museum merged with the British Columbia Provincial Archives in 2003.

names.ja: ロイヤル・ブリティッシュコロンビア博物館

spots.name: Fan Tan Alley
spots.summary: Fan Tan Alley is an alley in the Chinatown neighbourhood of Victoria, British Columbia, Canada that is known for being the narrowest commercial street in North America, being less than 0.9 m (3.0 ft) wide at its narrowest point.

spots.name: Fort Victoria

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Fort Victoria began as a fur trading post of the Hudson's Bay Company and was the headquarters of HBC operations in the Columbia District, a large fur trading area now part of the province of British Columbia, Canada and the U.S. state of Washington.

spots.name: Fisgard Lighthouse
spots.summary: Fisgard Lighthouse National Historic Site, on Fisgard Island at the mouth of Esquimalt Harbour in Colwood, British Columbia, is the site of Fisgard Lighthouse, the first lighthouse on the west coast of Canada.

spots.name: Beacon Hill Park
spots.summary: Beacon Hill Park is a 75 ha park located along the shore of Juan de Fuca Strait in Victoria, British Columbia that is popular both with tourists and locals.

spots.name: Fort Rodd Hill National Historic Site

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Fort Rodd Hill National Historic Site is a 19th-century coastal artillery fort located on Esquimalt Harbour in Colwood, British Columbia, Canada. It was constructed in the 1890s by the Royal Marine Artillery to defend the Esquimalt Naval Base.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Fort Rodd Hill National Historic Site

names.fr: Lieu historique national fort Rodd Hill

spots.name: St. Andrew's Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Andrew's Cathedral is the Roman Catholic cathedral for the Diocese of Victoria in British Columbia, Canada. Built in the High Victorian Gothic style, St. Andrew's was Victoria's third cathedral to be built.

photo.author: Original uploader was Drhaggis at en.wikipedia

spots.name: Thunderbird Park
spots.summary: Thunderbird Park in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada, is next to the Royal British Columbia Museum and home to many totem poles and other First Nation monuments. The park takes its name from the mythological Thunderbird of Indigenous North American cultures, which is depicted on many totem poles.

spots.name: Munro's Books
spots.summary: Munro's Books is a large independent bookstore in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada, located in a landmark heritage building on Government Street. It was founded in 1963 by Jim Munro and his then-wife Alice. Since Jim's retirement in 2014, the store has had no connection to the Munro family.

spots.name: Statue of Queen Victoria
spots.summary: The statue of Queen Victoria is a bronze sculpture depicting Queen Victoria by British artist Albert Bruce-Joy, installed outside the British Columbia Parliament Buildings, in Victoria, British Columbia. The 4-metre (13 ft) statue was commissioned by Richard McBride in 1912, and completed in 1914.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Statue of Queen Victoria (Victoria, British Columbia)

spots.name: Pacific Undersea Gardens
spots.summary: The Pacific Undersea Gardens was located at the Inner Harbour in the heart of downtown Victoria. The Gardens were owned and operated by the Oak Bay Marine Group.

spots.name: Statue of James Cook
spots.summary: A statue of Captain James Cook stood in Victoria, British Columbia, from 1976 until 2021, when it was toppled in a protest. It was a fibreglass copy of a bronze statue of 1912 by John Tweed in Whitby, Yorkshire, England.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Statue of James Cook (Victoria, British Columbia)

spots.name: Gate of Harmonious Interest
spots.summary: The Gate of Harmonious Interest is a gate and cultural landmark located in Chinatown, Victoria, British Columbia. It spans Fisgard Street, west of Government Street. Erected in 1981, it was part of the revitalization efforts of Chinatown by the City of Victoria and the Chinese Consolidated Benevolent Association.

spots.name: Helmcken House

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Helmcken House is a museum in Victoria, British Columbia, located in Thunderbird Park. It was built in 1852 by Dr. John Sebastian Helmcken, a surgeon with the Hudson's Bay Company and the first doctor in Victoria when he married Cecilia Douglas, daughter of Governor James Douglas.

spots.name: Ross Bay Cemetery
spots.summary: Ross Bay Cemetery is located at 1516 Fairfield Road in Victoria, British Columbia, on Vancouver Island, Canada. Many historical figures from the early days of the province and colony of British Columbia are buried at Ross Bay.

photo.author: Brandon Godfrey from Victoria B.C, Canada

spots.name: Bastion Square
spots.summary: Bastion Square is a historic pedestrian mall in Victoria, British Columbia.

spots.name: Johnson Street Bridge
spots.summary: The Johnson Street Bridge is a bascule bridge spanning the Victoria Harbour in Victoria, British Columbia. Four known bridges have spanned the narrows between Victoria's Inner Harbour and Upper Harbour, connecting Johnson Street on the east shore with Esquimalt Road on the west shore.

spots.name: Netherlands Centennial Carillon

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Netherlands Centennial Carillon is a 62-bell carillon located in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada. Its tower is located at the intersection of Government Street and Belleville Street, in front of the Royal British Columbia Museum and across the street from the Parliament Building.

spots.name: Victoria City Hall
spots.summary: Victoria City Hall is the city hall for Victoria, British Columbia, Canada. It is located at the corner of Douglas Street and Pandora Avenue adjacent to the CTV Vancouver Island studios and the McPherson Playhouse in downtown Victoria. It is home to the Victoria City Council. It was completed in 1890.

spots.name: Douglas Obelisk
spots.summary: Douglas Obelisk is an 8-metre (27 ft) marble obelisk, installed outside the British Columbia Parliament Buildings in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada.

spots.name: Centennial Square
spots.summary: Centennial Square is a plaza in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada. It was built to celebrate the 100th anniversary of the incorporation of the City of Victoria. The Victoria Police Station, City Hall, and McPherson Playhouse are adjacent to the square. There is a fountain in the square.

spots.name: Greater Victoria Public Library
spots.summary: The Greater Victoria Public Library (GVPL) is a public library that serves Victoria, British Columbia and the surrounding area.

spots.name: British Columbia Legislature Cenotaph
spots.summary: The British Columbia Legislature Cenotaph, also known as the Victoria Cenotaph and the War Memorial to the Unknown Soldier, is a war memorial, installed outside the British Columbia Parliament Buildings in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada. Unveiled by Lt.-Gov. W.C.

spots.name: St. Ann's Academy
spots.summary: St. Ann's Academy, in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada, was a girls' Catholic boarding and day school from grades 1–12, and boys K–3, though boys stopped being admitted in the 1950s. First Nations orphans and girls were sent to the Academy from other missions run by the Sisters of St. Ann.

spots.name: Maritime Museum of BC

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Maritime Museum of British Columbia (MMBC) is a museum in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada, that engages people with the maritime culture and history of the Pacific Northwest through rotating exhibits, educational and community-based programs, research services, and more.

spots.name: Church of Our Lord

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of Our Lord, built in 1866-1870 and is located at 626 Blanshard Street in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada, is an historic Carpenter Gothic church that is designated as a National Historic Site of Canada.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of Our Lord (Victoria, British Columbia)

spots.name: Congregation Emanu-El

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Congregation Emanu-El is a Conservative synagogue located in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada. The congregation is affiliated with the United Synagogue of Conservative Judaism.

spots.name: Confederation Garden Court
spots.summary: Confederation Garden Court is a plaza in Victoria, British Columbia, completed in 1967 to commemorate the Canadian Centennial of confederation. The plaza features the British Columbia Time Capsule and Confederation Fountain, and is maintained by the Legislative Assembly of British Columbia.

spots.name: Chinese Consolidated Benevolent Association and Chinese Public School
spots.summary: The Chinese Consolidated Benevolent Association and Victoria Chinese Public School is a historic building located in the downtown core of Victoria, British Columbia, Canada.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Chinese Consolidated Benevolent Association and Chinese Public School

names.zh: 加拿大域多利中華會館

spots.name: St. Andrew's Presbyterian Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Andrew's Presbyterian Church is a Presbyterian church in downtown Victoria, British Columbia, Canada. The congregation was founded in 1862 and the current church building was completed in 1890.
spots.wikipediaTitle: St. Andrew's Presbyterian Church (Victoria, British Columbia)

spots.name: Old Victoria Custom House
spots.summary: The Old Victoria Custom House, also known as the Malahat Building, in Victoria was completed in 1875 and designated as a historic building in 1987.

names.fr: Ancien édifice de la douane de Victoria

spots.name: 100th Anniversary of the Canadian Navy
spots.summary: 100th Anniversary of the Canadian Navy is an outdoor memorial in Victoria, British Columbia. It was constructed to commemorate the founding of the Royal Canadian Navy and opened on the date of the navy's centenary.

spots.name: Royal Theatre
spots.summary: The Royal Theatre is a proscenium arch theatre and concert hall located in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada. It was designed in 1912 by William D'Oyly Hamilton Rochfort and Eben W. Sankey. Rochfort was very active as an architect in Victoria from 1908 until he left for the war in 1914.

photo.author: Ryan Bushby aka H aka HighInBC aka Chillum at en.wikipedia

spots.name: Front Fountain
spots.summary: Front Fountain is a fountain designed by Hooper & Watkins, installed outside the British Columbia Parliament Buildings, in Victoria, British Columbia. It was manufactured in 1905, by Joseph W. Fiske in New York, and installed in 1906. The fountain has one large ceramic tile basin with a granite rim.

spots.name: Rogers Building
spots.summary: Rogers Building or Rogers Chocolates is a historic building in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada, it is located at 913 Government Street in downtown Victoria.

spots.name: Victoria Centennial Fountain
spots.summary: Victoria Centennial Fountain, also known as Back Fountain or simply Centennial Fountain, is installed outside the British Columbia Parliament Buildings in Victoria, British Columbia.

spots.name: University of Victoria Legacy Art Galleries

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The University of Victoria Legacy Art Galleries (Legacy) is the university's art museum in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada, responsible for the accessibility and stewardship of an art collection which consists of approximately 18,000 objects including Canadian, Indigenous and international historic and contemporary art.
spots.wikipediaTitle: University of Victoria Legacy Art Galleries

spots.name: Causeway Tower and Garage
spots.summary: The Causeway Tower and Garage is an historic building in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada. Originally built in 1930-31 as a service centre for the Imperial Oil Company, it is now a visitors centre, gift shop and a restaurant.

spots.name: Masonic Temple
spots.summary: The Masonic Template is an historic building in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada.

photo.author: Joe Mabel (on Flickr as Joe Mabel from Seattle, US)

spots.name: Bank of Montreal Building
spots.summary: The Bank of Montreal Building, or Bank of Montreal, Government Street Branch, is an historic building in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada. Designed by architect Francis Rattenbury, the building was constructed in 1897.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Bank of Montreal Building (Victoria, British Columbia)

spots.name: Ocean Island Inn
spots.summary: Ocean Island Inn is a historic building in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada; it is Vancouver Island's largest backpackers' inn.

photo.author: Joe Mabel (on Flickr as Joe Mabel from Seattle, US)

spots.name: Odd Fellows Hall
spots.summary: Odd Fellows Hall is a historic building in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada. It is located at the intersection of Wharf Street and Fort Street in downtown Victoria, and it is now the location of The Keg restaurant.

spots.name: City Hall Annex
spots.summary: City Hall Annex is an historic building in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada.

spots.name: Lim Dat Building
spots.summary: The Lim Dat Building is an historic building in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada. Built in 1898, it stands at the corner of Store and Fisgard Streets on the edge of Victoria's Chinatown area.

spots.name: Loo Tai Cho Building
spots.summary: The Loo Tai Cho Building is an historic building in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada.

photo.author: Joe Mabel (on Flickr as Joe Mabel from Seattle, US)

spots.name: Central Branch of Greater Victoria Public Library

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Central Branch of the Greater Victoria Public Library (GVPL) is the system's main branch, located at 735 Broughton Street in the downtown core of Victoria, British Columbia, Canada. The Heritage Room includes a special collection with approximately 2,500 items related to the history of Vancouver Island.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Central Branch of Greater Victoria Public Library

spots.name: Gee Tuck Tong Benevolent Association Building
spots.summary: The Gee Tuck Tong Benevolent Association Building is an historic building in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Gee Tuck Tong Benevolent Association Building

photo.author: Joe Mabel (on Flickr as Joe Mabel from Seattle, US)

spots.name: Fairfield Block
spots.summary: Fairfield Block is a historic building in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada. It was completed in 1912 and has a total of three floors. Designed by architect Henry Sandham Griffith, the building is a notable example of Edwardian commercial architecture.

photo.author: Joe Mabel (on Flickr as Joe Mabel from Seattle, US)

spots.name: Adelphi Building
spots.summary: The Adelphi Building is an historic building in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada. It is located on the northwest corner of Government and Yates Streets.

spots.name: Mark Loria Gallery

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Mark Loria Gallery is a Canadian contemporary art gallery specializing in Northwest Coast, Coast Salish, and Canadian indigenous fine art. The gallery exhibits artwork from the contemporary period as well as representing over 60 current artists.

spots.name: Pacific Transfer Building
spots.summary: The Pacific Transfer Building is an historic building in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada. It was owned by The Pacific Transfer Company, a company that offered express deliveries within the City of Victoria and was key in the distribution of goods arriving by ship and rail.

spots.name: Rithet Building
spots.summary: The Rithet Building is an historic building in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada. It is a three-storey brick commercial building on the east side of Wharf Street, facing Victoria's Inner Harbour.

photo.author: Joe Mabel (on Flickr as Joe Mabel from Seattle, US)

spots.name: British Columbia Law Enforcement Memorial
spots.summary: The British Columbia Law Enforcement Memorial is a memorial commemorating law enforcement professionals who died in the line of duty, in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada.

spots.name: Milne Block
spots.summary: Milne Block is an historic building in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada, located at 546-548 Johnson Street, just west of Wharf Street.

spots.name: New England Hotel
spots.summary: The New England Hotel is an historic building in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada.

spots.name: Duck's Block
spots.summary: The Duck's Block is an historic building in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada.

spots.name: Hudson's Bay Company Department Store
spots.summary: The Hudson's Bay Company Department Store is an historic building in Victoria, British Columbia, Canada. It is currently being used as a public market space.

photo.author: Joe Mabel (on Flickr as Joe Mabel from Seattle, US)

spots.name: Fallen Paramedics Memorial
spots.summary: The Fallen Paramedics Memorial is a monument commemorating paramedics who have died in the line of duty, installed in Victoria, British Columbia. The memorial was unveiled on May 6, 2015. It is located in the BC Emergency Services Garden of Honour, south of the Legislative Buildings.
